blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object holds AWS settings for a load balancer. It comes from the eks.amazonaws.com API.
blocks.why: An Ingress routes web requests by host name and path. Auto Mode serves it with an Application Load Balancer.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: AWS settings for the load balancer, from EKS Auto Mode’s own API

blocks.title: Public, please
blocks.what: The settings are called public-alb. scheme: internet-facing makes the load balancer reachable from the internet.
blocks.why: Auto Mode reads AWS settings from here, not from annotations on the IngressClass.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the object, because it needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing

blocks.title: Name a class of Ingress
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: an IngressClass called public-alb.
blocks.why: An IngressClass says which controller serves Ingresses that name it. A cluster can have several.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb

blocks.title: Auto Mode serves it
blocks.what: controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb hands this class to Auto Mode. parameters points to the AWS settings above.
blocks.why: One class can serve many Ingresses, all with the same AWS settings.
blocks.ifRemoved: No controller serves the class, so no load balancer is created.
blocks.comment: Auto Mode creates load balancers for this class, using the settings above
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb
  parameters:
    apiGroup: eks.amazonaws.com
    kind: IngressClassParams
    name: public-alb

blocks.title: Add the Ingress
blocks.what: Three dashes start a third object: an Ingress called web.
blocks.why: The Ingress holds the routing rules. Each team can write its own.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A third object: the routing rules
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb
  parameters:
    apiGroup: eks.amazonaws.com
    kind: IngressClassParams
    name: public-alb
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web

blocks.title: Which class and which host?
blocks.what: ingressClassName picks public-alb. The rule matches requests for the host shop.example.com.
blocks.why: One load balancer can serve many sites, telling them apart by host name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Ingress, because a rule needs somewhere to send requests.
blocks.comment: Use the public-alb class, for requests to shop.example.com
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb
  parameters:
    apiGroup: eks.amazonaws.com
    kind: IngressClassParams
    name: public-alb
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  ingressClassName: public-alb
  rules:
    - host: shop.example.com

blocks.title: Which paths?
blocks.what: path: / with pathType: Prefix matches every path that starts with /, which is all of them.
blocks.why: You could send /api to one Service and / to another.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the rule, because it needs at least one path.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb
  parameters:
    apiGroup: eks.amazonaws.com
    kind: IngressClassParams
    name: public-alb
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  ingressClassName: public-alb
  rules:
    - host: shop.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix

blocks.title: Send it to the Service
blocks.what: Matching requests go to the web Service on port 80, from the ClusterIP lesson. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: The load balancer reaches the Pods behind that Service directly, by their IP addresses.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the path, because it needs a backend.
blocks.comment: Send matching requests to the web Service on port 80
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: IngressClassParams
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  scheme: internet-facing
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: public-alb
spec:
  controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb
  parameters:
    apiGroup: eks.amazonaws.com
    kind: IngressClassParams
    name: public-alb
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  ingressClassName: public-alb
  rules:
    - host: shop.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web
                port:
                  number: 80

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version. IngressClassParams is Auto Mode’s own; the others are networking.k8s.io/v1.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.IngressClassParams:kind: AWS settings for every load balancer made for one IngressClass.
notes.IngressClass:kind: A class of Ingress, and the controller that serves it.
notes.Ingress:kind: Routing rules for web requests, by host name and path.
notes.IngressClassParams:metadata.name: The settings’ name. The IngressClass points to it.
notes.IngressClass:metadata.name: The class name. Ingresses choose it with ingressClassName.
notes.Ingress:metadata.name: The Ingress name. kubectl get ingress web shows its address.
notes.IngressClass:spec: Who serves this class, and with which settings.
notes.Ingress:spec: Which class serves it, and the routing rules.
notes.spec.scheme: internet-facing: reachable from the internet. internal: only from inside your VPC.
notes.spec.controller: eks.amazonaws.com/alb: EKS Auto Mode creates an Application Load Balancer.
notes.spec.parameters: Where the class’s AWS settings live.
notes.spec.parameters.name: The settings’ name: public-alb, the first object in this file.
notes.spec.ingressClassName: Which IngressClass serves this Ingress: public-alb.
notes.spec.rules: Routing rules. Each list item matches one host.
notes.spec.rules[].host: Requests for shop.example.com. A placeholder: use a domain you own.
notes.spec.rules[].http: Rules for web requests to this host.
notes.spec.rules[].http.paths: Paths to match. Each list item sends one path to one Service.
notes.spec.rules[].http.paths[].pathType: Prefix: any path starting with /. Exact matches one path only.
notes.spec.rules[].http.paths[].backend.servic: A Service in the same namespace.
The web Service from the ClusterIP lesson.
Port 80, where the web Service listens.

questions.question: Which object makes the load balancer public?
questions.explain: Auto Mode reads AWS settings, such as the scheme, from IngressClassParams.

questions.question: A request arrives for shop.example.com/cart. Where does it go?
answers: To the web Service: Prefix / matches every path
questions.explain: Prefix / matches /cart and every other path.

questions.question: Who creates the Application Load Balancer?
answers: EKS Auto Mode, named by controller
questions.explain: The IngressClass hands its Ingresses to the eks.amazonaws.com/alb controller, which is Auto Mode.

fix.message: Ingress in version "v1" cannot be handled as a Ingress: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.kubernetes.io/ingress.class"
fix.explain: kubernetes.io/ingress.class is the old annotation, and it never belonged under spec. Kubernetes now uses spec.ingressClassName.
